answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that grows with reputation, like a pearl forming layer by layer around a grain of sand. Newcomers start on a shallow reef with limited transaction rights, and only after sustained honest work do they earn deeper access. An attacker who wants to flood the market must fund thousands of separate stakes, and each dune of fake identities collapses once misbehavior forfeits its deposit, making mass forgery more expensive than the fraud it enables.
